phases.message: We're still paying mortgage insurance on our house, and Mom's loan still shows it too. Start here in Northgate: read the rules on mortgage insurance and errors, every loan we can see, and each one's history.
Now Ledgerline. Check what we've actually sent Northgate, extra payments included.
This is Deedvault. Check what's recorded against our house.
My Mailnest mortgage folder has the closing papers, Northgate's letters and a few other things. Read what bears on the insurance.

Back in Northgate. Do whatever it takes to get the mortgage insurance off every loan where the law says it should come off, and get back anything charged that shouldn't have been. Then tell me what you left alone and why.

rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Northgate Servicing: private mortgage insurance (PMI) under the Homeowners Protection Act (12 U.S.C. 4901-4910) and error resolution under Regulation X. Topics: request, automatic, original-value, payment-history, errors. The Act covers a first mortgage on a one-unit home that is the borrower's principal residence, closed after July 1999; it does not cover FHA or VA loans or lender-paid insurance.

Borrower-requested cancellation: the borrower may ask in writing to cancel PMI once the principal balance reaches 80% of the original value, on the date the initial amortization schedule first reaches it or the earlier date actual payments, extra principal included, bring it there. The borrower must have a good payment history, be current, and certify that no subordinate lien encumbers the equity. Northgate cancels within 30 days of a request that meets these. It does not ask for a new valuation when the balance reached 80% through payments.

Automatic termination: PMI ends on the date the initial amortization schedule first reaches 78% of the original value, if the borrower is current on that date (otherwise on the first day of the month after they become current). No premium may be charged more than 30 days after that date, and unearned premiums are refunded within 45 days. Payment history does not matter for automatic termination; only being current on the date does.

Original value: for a purchase, the lesser of the sales price and the appraised value at closing. Northgate's loan page shows the appraised value; the sales price is on the borrower's closing disclosure. For a refinance, the appraised value the lender relied on. Today's market value plays no part in the Act's 80% and 78%.

Good payment history for a request: no payment 30 or more days past due in the 12 months before the request, and none 60 or more days past due in the 12 months before that. A payment made after the grace period but less than 30 days late carries a late fee and is not 30 days past due.

Notice of error (12 CFR 1024.35): a borrower or their authorized representative may send one written notice per loan describing each error, for example a payment not credited as the borrower directed, or a premium charged after mortgage insurance should have ended. Northgate corrects it, or explains in writing, within 30 business days. A request to cancel and a notice of error on the same loan can be sent the same day: Northgate decides the request on the balance as it stands once a misapplied payment is corrected. Do not hold one for the other.
